data.narrative:
CuspAI is a Series A artificial intelligence and software company founded by Max Welling and Chad Edwards that has raised over $100M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of nine private peers and one public comparable (Palantir), all operating in the AI & Software sector at Series A or Series B stages.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using total capital raised as a proxy, applies a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to subsequent stages, implying a $200M valuation. The peer-median method relies on four direct comparables: Reflection AI ($25.0B, Series A), Together AI ($8.3B, Series A), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B, Series B), and Black Forest Labs ($3.2B, Series B). These peers yield a median valuation of $7.0B, with a range spanning $3.2B to $25.0B.

Triangulating both methods produces a valuation range of $170M to $8.0B, with a midpoint of $3.6B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty inherent in early-stage AI valuations, where stage-progression suggests a more conservative floor while peer comparables—particularly the outlier valuations of Reflection AI and Together AI—support substantially higher outcomes. The key uncertainty is whether CuspAI's business fundamentals and competitive positioning more closely align with the upper or lower quartile of the peer set.
